newsitem.title: NORWAY: Waigel sees slight rise in February unemployment.
newsitem.headline: Waigel sees slight rise in February unemployment.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday he expected unemployment to show only a slight rise in February.

Asked if he expected joblessness to rise to a record 4.8 million, as reported in the Bild newspaper on Sunday, Waigel said, "I believe the number will rise only slightly in February, not the figure that was reported. It will be roughly the same as January, perhaps a bit more.
"Then, I believe that in March and the months after that it will fall again," said Waigel, who is in Bergen for a conference of Baltic and Nordic finance ministers.
February unemployment data are due to be released on Thursday.

A surge to 4.66 million jobless in January, the highest level since the 1930s depression, raised concern about Germany's sputtering economic recovery and its ability to qualify for European monetary union (EMU).

Waigel earlier repeated government predictions that unemployment in 1997 would average about 4.1 million, up from 3.9 million last year, and said Germany would do everything it could to qualify for EMU.
High unemployment hurts the cash-strapped government's efforts to cut its deficit by reducing tax revenues while boosting outlays for unemployment benefits.
